skill.name: trpc-scaffolder
skill.description: Scaffolds tRPC routers, procedures, and Zod schemas for TypeScript projects using project-specific templates and validation helpers.
skill.summary: Generate tRPC endpoint scaffolding with routers, procedures, Zod schemas, and validation checks.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code examples, relative TypeScript imports, and intended .claude skill paths. One semantic issue remains: Bash helpers accept raw scaffold names and use them in generated file paths without validation. The author should constrain names and verify canonical output paths before publication.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated router, entity, and procedure names
remediation.suggestion: Reject names that do not match a strict identifier pattern, such as letters followed by letters or digits. Block dots, slashes, whitespace, shell metacharacters, and traversal tokens.

remediation.issue: Generated output paths are not canonicalized
remediation.suggestion: Resolve each output path with realpath or an equivalent canonical check, then verify it remains inside the intended routers or schemas directory before writing.

remediation.issue: Template replacements do not escape sed replacement values
remediation.suggestion: Escape replacement values before passing them to sed, or use a small structured templating script that treats names as data.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Scaffold Names Can Escape Intended Paths
semantic_findings.description: create-router.sh and create-schema.sh place raw command arguments into output filenames, and add-procedure.sh uses the raw router name when selecting a router file. Names containing path separators or traversal tokens can target files outside the intended routers and schemas directories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts derive OUTPUT_FILE or ROUTER_FILE directly from positional arguments without a whitelist or canonical-path check. The issue requires attacker-controlled scaffold names, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent tRPC routers and Zod schemas takes repetitive setup work. This skill provides scripts, templates, and examples for project-aligned endpoint scaffolding.
actual_capabilities: Creates tRPC router files from a reusable TypeScript template.
Generates Zod schema files with inferred TypeScript type exports.
Produces procedure snippets for query and mutation workflows.
Checks router registration and schema type export conventions.
Provides quick-start, pattern, and example files for tRPC implementation.
limitations: Assumes the DevPrep AI frontend path layout and tRPC folder names.
Requires Bash and a TypeScript project that already uses tRPC and Zod.
Does not implement endpoint business logic or database integration.
Generated files still need review, imports, and router registration.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Endpoint
use_cases.description: Create a new router, schema, and starter procedure for a product feature with consistent project structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Patterns
use_cases.description: Use the included examples and validation script to align endpoint code with existing tRPC conventions.

use_cases.title: Learn Project tRPC Flow
use_cases.description: Follow the quick-start guide to understand schemas, routers, procedures, and frontend usage together.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Router
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new domain router.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tRPC scaffolder to create a new router for users. Show me the generated file path and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Add validation types for a new entity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tRPC scaffolder to create a Zod schema for interview hints. Include what fields I should customize after generation.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Procedure
prompt_templates.scenario: Extend an existing router with a query or mutation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tRPC scaffolder to add a query procedure named getHints to the ai router. Explain where the snippet should go.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Repair Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after multiple endpoint changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tRPC scaffolder validation flow to check router registration and schema exports. Identify any missing steps and propose fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a user router for profile endpoints.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a user router file in the project router directory and lists the registration steps for the app router.

output_examples.input: Create a hint schema for a new endpoint.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a hint schema file, adds starter validation exports, and explains which placeholders need real fields.

output_examples.input: Validate the tRPC setup after adding files.
output_examples.output: The skill checks for app router registration, router files, schema files, and exported inferred types, then reports follow-up actions.

best_practices: Use simple alphanumeric names for routers, procedures, and schemas.
Review generated schemas before connecting procedures to business logic.
Run the validation script after creating or editing tRPC files.
anti_patterns: Do not use untrusted or path-like text as scaffold names.
Do not skip router registration after creating a new router file.
Do not leave placeholder schema fields in production endpoints.

faq.question: What projects does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets TypeScript projects that use tRPC, Zod, and the DevPrep AI folder layout.

faq.question: Does it write endpoint business logic?
faq.answer: No. It creates structure, templates, schemas, snippets, and validation guidance for developers to complete.

faq.question: Can it add both queries and mutations?
faq.answer: Yes. The procedure helper accepts query or mutation as the procedure type.

faq.question: Does it register routers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prints the required registration steps and the validation script checks the result.

faq.question: Why are Zod schemas included?
faq.answer: Zod schemas provide runtime validation and inferred TypeScript types for tRPC input and output data.

faq.question: What should I review after generation?
faq.answer: Review scaffold names, placeholder fields, imports, output schemas, authorization, and business logic before committing changes.
